assets.role: Complete public Titanic labeled training dataset mirror, 891 records and 12 columns

simulation: Page 01 first measures elephant depth 44 cm, retaining unknown weight. Only six stones of 250 kg are available (1500 kg), producing ideal physical depth 24 cm. Observations share the small measurement offsets used on pages 02–04. No extra stone can be added after six; weight is inferred on page 02. The shortage and values are invented teaching modifications, not historical claims.
page02Simulation: Six calibration masses 250–1500 kg with small symmetric measurement offsets; fitted trend has slope 0.016 cm/kg. Inverting target depth 44 cm estimates 2750 kg. Invented teaching values, not historical measurements.
physicsModel: Constant horizontal waterplane area A=6.25 m², water density rho=1000 kg/m³, displacement change Delta V=A Delta h, added mass m=rho A Delta h. Hence ideal Delta h=0.016 cm/kg. Assumes upright stable flotation, uniform water density, waterline stays on the vertical-wall portion, no overflow or change in hull/other load. The illustrated boat is a teaching model, not a reconstruction of Cao Chong’s historical vessel.
